entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: Home News The Politics of Self Sabotage: Why Igala Must End Internal Battles Before Facing 2027. The Politics of Self Sabotage: Why Igala Must End Internal Battles Before Facing 2027. Yet for too long, Igala politics has resembled a house where its occupants keep widening the cracks in the foundation while expecting the roof to withstand every storm. As conversations around the 2027 elections gather momentum, the greatest threat to the Igala political future may not emerge from rival blocs or competing interests outside Kogi East. A people who continually dig political trenches for one another should not be surprised when they all struggle to cross them. Communities that command enduring political influence are rarely those with the largest populations or the loudest voices. The road to 2027 will test the political maturity of the Igala people. The time has come to fill the trenches instead of deepening them, to replace suspicion with strategic cooperation, and to recognise that no community rises by defeating itself.

entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: * Created On:  19 July 2026 9:18 AM IST. **Hanumakonda/ Hyderabad**: Warangal Member of Parliament Dr Kadiyam Kavya said that the Congress government is giving top priority to women’s welfare, economic self-reliance, and leadership development. She stated that the government is implementing several initiatives to provide women with equal opportunities in all sectors while promoting self-employment and entrepreneurship. Addressing the ‘Rise Her–2026’ Women’s Empowerment Conclave, organised by the Telangana SC/ST Industrial Chamber of Commerce (TSICC) at Red Hills in Hyderabad, Dr Kavya said that the Telangana government is firmly committed to women’s welfare, empowerment, and financial independence. She also noted that the State government is strengthening Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and encouraging savings, self-employment, and entrepreneurship among women. She said that when women confidently showcase their abilities and make effective use of the opportunities available to them, it will lead to the overall development of families, society, and the State.

BUDAPEST, Hungary (AP) — Hungary’s former prime minister Viktor Orbán declared on Wednesday that he and his far-right Fidesz party will lead a peaceful “resistance” movement against what he called the tyrannical exercise of power by the country’s new center-right government. At a news conference outside party headquarters in Budapest, Orbán said a constitutional amendment passed last week by Tisza’s majority in Parliament — which removed Hungary’s Orbán-era president and set a 12-year term limit for members of Parliament — had “dismantled the rule of law and eliminated the system of checks and balances.”. The new administration suspended the news service of Hungary’s public television and radio — which Magyar argued served as a “propaganda factory” for Orbán’s party — and closed the Sovereignty Protection Office, an authority seen by Orbán’s opponents as a tool for intimidating critics and silencing independent media.

entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: Home » News » Oyebamiji pledges agriculture-driven economy, mechanised farming for Osun. ## Oyebamiji pledges agriculture-driven economy, mechanised farming for Osun. OSOGBO — The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Osun State, Bola Oyebamiji, has promised to prioritise agriculture and mechanised farming as part of efforts to boost economic growth and improve livelihoods across the state if elected. The candidate said his administration would leverage Osun’s agricultural potential to transform the economy, create opportunities for rural communities and increase agricultural productivity. Addressing supporters in Ibokun after meeting with traditional rulers, Oyebamiji said agriculture remained one of the state’s major areas of comparative advantage. “One of my major plans is to develop the Osun economy using agriculture, where our state has comparative advantage. We will encourage mechanised farming in all agrarian communities to make farming easier, attractive and increase productivity,” he said. He added that his administration would complement agricultural development with improved rural infrastructure by constructing and rehabilitating roads to connect farming communities with markets.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Bold pledges, upbeat mood and informality: What we learned from Andy Burnham’s first day as Britain’s leader - CNN
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: Prime Minister Andy Burnham makes a speech outside 10 Downing Street, London, on Monday. Britain’s new Prime Minister Andy Burnham entered 10 Downing Street on Monday, making few detailed policy statements but offering plenty of clues about the nature of his premiership. Optics mean a great deal in politics, so on Burnham’s first day in the job, he delivered bold pledges, without constraining himself to timelines, showcased a more informal style of leadership and brought with him a more upbeat mood to Downing Street. “I will soon go through that door behind me and issue my first instruction to end rough sleeping in our country,” he said at the end of his first address as prime minister. “The Prime Minister rejects the notion that ending rough sleeping will take decades or that it can’t be done at all,” a line in the accompanying statement said, illustrating the scope of Burnham’s ambition. entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # BEST To Invest Rs 6,500 Crore In 5,000 Self-Owned Electric Buses, Plans 10,000-Bus Fleet To Reduce Dependence On Wet-Lease Operations. BEST electric buses (BEST Bus Transport). The Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking has unveiled a long-term strategy to rebuild its own bus fleet, announcing plans to acquire 5,000 self-owned electric buses as part of a wider target of operating 10,000 buses across Mumbai over the next two to three years. The move marks a significant shift away from the wet-lease model that has dominated BEST's operations in recent years. Speaking after a BEST committee meeting, General Manager Sonia Sethi said the undertaking currently relies more on wet-lease buses than vehicles owned by the transport utility. While BEST currently operates around 2,800 buses and is set to induct 1,500 wet-lease electric buses under the Centre's PM e-Bus Scheme, officials said future fleet expansion will increasingly focus on company-owned vehicles beyond the scheme's support period ending in 2027.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: BEST gets state nod to buy 5,000 self-owned AC e-buses | Mumbai news - Hindustan Times
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # BEST gets state nod to buy 5,000 self-owned AC e-buses. Mumbai: After a decade, the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking has received the state government’s approval to procure 5,000 self-owned AC electric buses at an estimated cost of ₹6,500 crore, marking a major shift away from its dependence on the wet-lease model. “We have received the minutes of the meeting from the deputy chief minister’s office approving the procurement of 5,000 AC e-buses for our owned fleet. The buses will be self-owned, with drivers, as in the past, and will be procured at an estimated cost of ₹6,500 crore,” said Sonia Sethi, general manager, BEST. The procurement, expected to be completed over the next three to four years, is part of BEST’s long-term plan to build a fleet of 10,000 buses. Officials said BEST will now work on a financial model for the procurement, which is expected to be placed before the BEST Committee within the next month.
